subject: Post-call: implementation hypothesis + SDK gap assessment for MedMorph POC
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily@medmorph.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: implementation hypothesis + SDK gap assessment for MedMorph POC

Hi Emily — thanks again for your time today. I captured a short implementation hypothesis and a list of SDK/feature gaps we should address before a tight POC. Please skim and confirm anything I missed.

High-level goals you stated
- Extract structured clinical summaries from provider notes and map to your internal taxonomy (SNOMED-lite).
- Nearby retrieval and reranking for patient-similarity lookups at latency < 250ms p95.
- Minimal PHI exposure: model inferencing must run within your VPC for the pilot.

Primary pain points mentioned
- Current NER pipeline misses nested entities and has brittle rules for medication/dosage.
- Embedding search has high variance when queries are long (~2–3x token length).
- Existing infra can’t support streaming token-level scoring for interactive review workflows.

Implementation hypothesis (what Redwood would deliver for the POC)
1) Private VPC deployment of Redwood Private with a dedicated inference pool (single-region) to meet PHI requirements.
2) Inference variant using function-calling + structured output schema for clinical summary extraction. We suggest forcing output to a compact JSON schema (we’ll validate with your taxonomy).
3) Embedding + rerank flow: Redwood embeddings for indexing + a 2-stage reranker (coarse ANN + model-based rerank) to improve recall for longer queries.
4) Streaming option: streaming tokens + intermediate rerank scores so your UI can show progressive results; fall back to batch for long queries.

SDK/feature gaps we noted (actionable items)
- SDK: Need a helper for schema-enforced function call generation and client-side validation (we’ll prototype).
- Streaming: small change to the JS SDK to surface partial rerank scores (Ben to propose patch).
- Embeddings: configuration presets for long-query truncation vs sliding windows (we’ll share recommended heuristics).
- Ops: Doc-level audit logs (agree on retention) and a KMS key rotation playbook for your security team.

Proposed next steps
- We’ll drop a gap matrix and a one-page scope (attached). Ben will follow with a technical delta doc and a patch plan by EOD Wednesday.
- Emily, can you confirm the internal taxonomy sample (a 10–15 item list) by Thursday so we can wire the function schema?
- If procurement is ready, please share primary billing contact so we can prepare a short-term POC quote for VPC Dedicated during the call next week.

Attachments: medmorph_poc_scope_v1.pdf (overview), redwood_sdk_gap_matrix.xlsx (gap matrix - draft)

Thanks — short and pragmatic.

—Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com

From: Emily Park <emily@medmorph.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Dunn <mark.dunn@medmorph.com>, procurement@medmorph.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: implementation hypothesis + SDK gap assessment for MedMorph POC

Thanks Stephanie — this matches my notes and is super helpful. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) Taxonomy: I’ll upload a sample 12-item taxonomy (conditions + procedures) by Thursday EOD to the Drive link you provided.
2) PHI: We need audit logs with 90-day retention and a KMS integration; our security team will want to validate the attestation before kickoff.
3) Latency target: 250ms p95 for the similarity endpoints is what we need for the clinician UI. If the streaming path is slightly slower, that’s ok as long as final rerank completes within 350ms.

Procurement: looping in procurement@medmorph.com — we’re open to a short-term Dedicated seat for the POC. Emily (procurement) — can you confirm approval cadence and PO contact?

Happy to run a short technical sync with your infra/security next Tue. Mark — are you available 6/23 for a 30-min alignment?

—Emily Park
Head of Product
MedMorph Health
emily@medmorph.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily@medmorph.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: implementation hypothesis + SDK gap assessment for MedMorph POC

Emily / team — quick technical follow-up and proposed owner-level split. I attached a draft gap matrix (redwood_sdk_gap_matrix.xlsx) with concrete diffs. Highlights: 

- SDK schema helper: we can ship a ~3-file JS/TS helper that wraps function-calling and validates against your taxonomy-derived JSON schema. Effort: ~3 dev-days + 1 day test. Owner: Ben (eng + SDK).
- Streaming partial scores: small API addition to our stream envelope (adds "score_delta" events). Effort: ~2 dev-days + doc. Owner: Ben (runtime + SDK).
- Embedding presets: we will produce a recommended set of vectorization knobs (window stride, pooling) for long queries; minimal infra change. Effort: 1–2 dev-days. Owner: Rishi (ML infra).
- VPC deployment checklist: security items and KMS rotation notes included. Effort: Ops kickstart + security review (~1 week). Owner: Stephanie + Security.

Action items and dates
- Ben: push SDK helper proposal and a PR draft by Wed EOD (2026-06-17).
- Rishi: share embedding presets and expected recall lift by Thu (2026-06-18).
- Stephanie: schedule security sync for Tue 2026-06-23 and share deployment checklist with MedMorph security.
- Emily: upload taxonomy sample by Thu (2026-06-18).
- procurement@medmorph.com: provide PO contact and cadence by Tue 2026-06-16.

Attachment: redwood_sdk_gap_matrix.xlsx (draft with effort estimates)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the PR link when ready.

—Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: implementation hypothesis + SDK gap assessment for MedMorph POC

Quick note — confirming I’ll draft the embedding presets and run a small simulation on a 2k-note sample to validate recall at different window strides. ETA: Thu 06/18 EOD. If that passes we should see a clear improvement in long-query recall without adding infra.

Also — I’ll include a brief recommended quantization profile for the reranker to keep memory usage low in VPC deployment.
